sources.title: David Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge), lecture notes
sources.locator: Sections read: Ch. 1 introduction (printed pp. 1-2, cross-product identities); §2.5.4 central forces / the effective potential (printed pp. 31-33, Eqs. (2.82)-(2.90)); §2.6 small oscillations (printed pp. 38-44); §4.5.1-4.5.3 action-angle variables (printed pp. 105-111, Eqs. (4.133)-(4.142)).

contents.name: §2.5.4 two-body reduction, conserved J = mu r^2 phidot, radial equation and effective potential (2.82)-(2.89)
contents.support: The item's central-force equation, angular momentum j, energy and effective potential are the coordinate-free form of this reduction; the printed equations are the source of the conventions.

contents.name: §2.5.4 planar polar coordinates and the angular first integral (2.83)-(2.84)
contents.support: The local lift of a planar curve to polar data is the twice-differentiable version of the polar substitution used here; the item adds the local construction and its uniqueness.

contents.name: §2.5.4 the orbit lies in the plane perpendicular to J and r^2 phidot is constant (2.83)-(2.84)
contents.support: The printed conservation statement is proved as a theorem for twice differentiable central-force trajectories, with the orthogonality statements added.

contents.name: §2.5.4 polar Lagrangian, radial equation and energy E = (1/2) mu rdot^2 + V_eff(r) (2.83)-(2.88)
contents.support: The item proves the same identities by direct differentiation, including the exact hypotheses on the interval and the definition of the polar data.

contents.name: §2.5.4 circular, elliptic and hyperbolic orbits as features of V_eff, Figure 15
contents.support: The circular-orbit condition and its radial quadratic reduction are the exact statement behind this figure discussion; only the linearised equation is claimed.

contents.name: §2.5.4 orbit equation for r(phi) and inverse-square radial equation (printed pp. 32-33)
contents.support: Binet's equation u''+u = mu kappa/J^2 is the item's clause; the source's derivation is by the substitution u = 1/r, which the item proves with the derivative-of-an-inverse and chain rules.

contents.name: §2.5.4 elliptic versus hyperbolic orbit classes via the sign of the energy (printed pp. 32-33)
contents.support: The item proves the conic form and the eccentricity-energy relation E = (mu kappa^2/(2J^2))(e^2-1), which is the quantitative version of this classification.

contents.name: §2.5.4 the E<0 elliptic branch (2.86)-(2.90)
contents.support: The completeness and periodicity statements of the item use this branch description together with the compact-continuation supplier; the period value is proved locally.

contents.name: §4.5.3 action variable I = (1/2 pi) oint p dq and the identity omega = dE/dI (4.133)-(4.142)
contents.support: The definition J_a(E) = (1/pi) int sqrt(2m(E-U)) dq is the twice-the-area normalisation of this action variable; the definition records the conversion J_a = I/2 explicitly (Tong Eq. (4.136) with I = J_a).

contents.name: §4.5.3 varying-endpoint cancellation and dE/dI = omega = 2 pi/T (4.136)-(4.142)
contents.support: The item proves the C^1 dependence of the turning points and the derivative J_a'(E) = T(E)/(2 pi) under exact simple-root hypotheses, using the inverse function theorem and differentiation under the integral sign.

contents.name: §4.5.1 harmonic oscillator action variable and period relation (printed pp. 105-111)
contents.support: The example evaluates the action variable and the period of the oscillator exactly, confirming the general derivative formula at this datum.

contents.name: §2.6 small oscillations and the general sinusoidal solution of v'' + omega^2 v = 0 (printed pp. 38-44)
contents.support: The item is the complete classification v(t) = A cos(omega(t-t0)) + B sin(omega(t-t0)) for the constant-coefficient second-order equation, proved from scratch.

contents.name: §1.1 vector triple product identity and orthonormal triad conventions (printed pp. 1-2)
contents.support: The component expansion u x (v x w) = <u,w> v - <u,v> w is proved by coordinates in the item.

contents.name: §1.1 and §2.5.4 oriented orthonormal triads, e1 x e2 = e3, planar coordinates
contents.support: The item constructs an oriented triad over any unit vector, proves the counting bound m <= 3 and the orthonormal expansion; these are the conventions behind the planar basis used in the notes.

contents.name: §2.5.4 angular-momentum barrier and separation of the radial and angular problems
contents.support: The counterexample exhibits the excluded radial J = 0 case and its finite-time collision, delimiting the region in which the planar polar reduction applies.

contents.name: Lagrangian and Noether machinery of Ch. 1 and Ch. 2
contents.reason: No item on this page uses the Lagrangian formalism; the polar reduction, Binet equation and action variable are proved directly from the second-order equations and the derivative calculus.

contents.name: §4 adiabatic invariants and the averaging arguments of §4.6
contents.reason: Only the exact one-dimensional action variable and its derivative are claimed here; adiabatic invariance requires a separate uniform chart and averaging hypotheses that are not part of this pair.

sources.title: Konstantin Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Classical Mechanics (Stony Brook University), full merged text
sources.locator: Chapters read: Ch. 2 small oscillations (second-order linear oscillator); §3.4 motion in a central field, Eqs. (3.44)-(3.65); §3.5 scattering, Eqs. (3.66)-(3.72); Ch. 10, §10.4 action variable of a periodic one-dimensional motion.

contents.name: §3.4 motion in a central field: first integral, polar coordinates, effective radial equation (3.44)-(3.57)
contents.support: The item proves the same identities (rho^2 theta' = J/mu, the radial equation, the energy) with explicit differentiability hypotheses and the local polar lift.

contents.name: §3.4 circular-orbit condition dU_eff/dr = 0 and small radial oscillations (3.52)-(3.58)
contents.support: The item states these as necessity, existence and linearised classification clauses, without claiming nonlinear stability.

contents.name: §3.4 Binet-type equation and the conic solution with eccentricity e for the Coulomb/Kepler potential (3.59)-(3.65)
contents.support: The item's conic form u = c(1 + e cos(phi - theta0)) and the eccentricity-energy relation are the exact statements behind this derivation.

contents.name: §3.4 elliptic branch E<0, e<1, turning radii, ellipse geometry and the period relation (3.59)-(3.65), Fig. 8
contents.support: The item proves the semiaxes a = p/(1-e^2), b = a sqrt(1-e^2), the identity E_ell = T[B] and the area pi ab with the Axiom of Countable Choice declared.

contents.name: §3.5 impact parameter, scattering angle, uniform-beam counting and the geometric cross-section relation (3.66)-(3.72)
contents.support: The incident flux measure, the solid-angle element, deflection branches and the density b|db/dtheta|/sin theta are the measure-theoretic form of the source's geometric counting, with the adopted-flux status stated.

contents.name: §3.5 nearest-approach point, equality of the two branch angle changes and the scattering-angle quadrature (3.66)-(3.68)
contents.support: The item develops the simple outer turning point, the two global branches and the free tails as a complete theorem under finite-range C^2 hypotheses.

contents.name: §3.5 L_z = b (2mE)^(1/2) for a scattering orbit (3.66)
contents.support: The item proves the existence of v_pm and the identity J = mu b |v_-| from the free tails and the energy identity.

contents.name: §3.5 theta = pi - 2 phi_0 with the nearest-approach angle (3.66)-(3.68)
contents.support: The advance quadrature Delta and the deflection relation modulo whole revolutions are the item's clauses.

contents.name: §3.5 the differential cross-section and b|db/dtheta|/sin theta (3.70)-(3.72)
contents.support: The item proves the substitution identity on a deflection branch and the additive density over finitely many disjoint branches.

contents.name: §3.5 scattering integral for the Coulomb potential, tan(theta/2) = alpha/(2Eb) (3.68)-(3.69)
contents.support: The item proves the strict monotonicity of V, the single simple turning point, global noncollision motion, the asymptotic velocities and the half-angle evaluation under repulsive-Coulomb hypotheses.

contents.name: §3.5 the Rutherford formula following Eq. (3.69)
contents.support: The item proves the deflection map and its inverse, the density (kappa/4E)^2 csc^4(theta/2) and the forward-angle divergence of the truncated total cross-section.

contents.name: Ch. 2 small oscillations: the second-order linear oscillator and its general sinusoidal solution
contents.support: The classification of solutions of v'' + omega^2 v = 0 is proved locally, not imported from the source's exposition.

contents.name: §10.4 adiabatic invariants and the action variable of a periodic one-dimensional motion
contents.support: Only the exact action variable and its energy derivative are used; the adiabatic-invariance discussion is motivation, and the item cites Ch. 10 for the definition's normalisation.

contents.name: Ch. 3 many-particle dynamics, scattering in the laboratory frame and the negative lab-density discussion
contents.reason: The pair treats the center-of-mass/relative formulation only; laboratory projectile angles and densities are a different formulation requiring the appropriate branch Jacobian, as the CM15 source review records.

contents.name: §3.6 the two-body problem with variable masses
contents.reason: Variable-mass accounting belongs to the balance pair cm-math-balances, not to the central-force reduction.

sources.title: Richard Fitzpatrick, Newtonian Dynamics (University of Texas at Austin), full book text
sources.locator: Complete book PDF (22649 extracted lines). Sections read: Ch. 2 §§2.4-2.5 and Appendix A (Cartesian components, orthonormal bases, cross-product and triple-product identities); Ch. 5 §§5.5-5.6 (Kepler orbit, semiaxes, focus); Ch. 6 §§6.2-6.5 (two-body reduction, general central force field, scattering in the center-of-mass frame and the Rutherford formula, Eq. (367) and following). The items cite the same sections in the official HTML presentation at Newtonhtml/node12.html, node44.html and node51.html; this single complete document is the fetch-verified full text.

contents.name: Impact parameter as the distance of closest approach in the absence of interaction, and the scattering angle as a decreasing function of it (Eqs. (340)-(347))
contents.support: The impact parameter and the branch picture are the geometric content of the definition; the item states the flux measure as adopted data and requires locally invertible branches. (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node51.html )

contents.name: Turning point quadrature and the two asymptotic branches of a scattering orbit (Eqs. (340)-(346))
contents.support: The item proves the simple outer turning point, global extension, quadrature and free tails under finite-range C^2 hypotheses. (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node51.html )

contents.name: Asymptotic velocity relation L = m v b (Eqs. (340)-(346))
contents.support: The item proves the existence of the asymptotic velocities and the identity J = mu b |v_-| by the free-tail and angular-momentum arguments. (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node51.html )

contents.name: Annular incident area 2 pi b db and outgoing solid-angle element sin theta dtheta dphi (Eqs. (347)-(351))
contents.support: The one-dimensional substitution identity and the density b|db/dtheta|/sin theta are the item's content; uniform incident flux remains an adopted preparation. (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node51.html )

contents.name: Rutherford scattering cross-section (367) and the divergence of the total cross-section at small angles (following (367))
contents.support: The item proves the density and the divergence of the truncated forward integral, and finiteness over every compact angular interval. (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node51.html )

contents.name: The assertion that the scattering angle is a decreasing function of the impact parameter for an arbitrary central potential
contents.reason: The local items require a smooth deflection branch with theta' ne 0 instead of a general monotonicity assertion; the CM15 review records this source limitation, and no item uses the general claim.
contents.support: (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node51.html )

contents.name: Shielding-dependent logarithmic total cross-section and laboratory-frame angle transformations
contents.reason: Neither shielding models nor laboratory-frame transformations are claimed; the ideal total cross-section divergence is proved for the truncated angular integral only.
contents.support: (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node51.html )

contents.name: Angular first integral r^2 thetadot = h in polar coordinates (299)-(304)
contents.support: The item proves the conserved angular momentum vector and its orthogonality; the scalar first integral is the J/mu normalization of the same statement. (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node44.html )

contents.name: Use of polar coordinates in the orbital plane
contents.support: The item supplies the twice differentiable local lift and its uniqueness, which this exposition assumes. (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node44.html )

contents.name: Cross-product identities including the vector triple product rule
contents.support: The item proves the triple product identity componentwise from the coordinate definition of the cross product. (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node12.html )

contents.name: Cartesian orthonormal bases and the scalar-product expansion a = (a.e1) e1 + (a.e2) e2
contents.support: The item proves the analogous expansion in an arbitrary oriented orthonormal triad and the bound that no four orthonormal vectors exist in R^3. (HTML presentation of this section: https://farside.ph.utexas.edu/teaching/336k/Newtonhtml/node12.html )

canonical.name: Finite-range scattering with a simple outer turning point: strict minimum, unique apsis, global branches, time quadrature and exactly free tails
canonical.support: Fitzpatrick and Likharev sketch the turning-point branch picture; the item states and proves the complete conditional theorem (V(r*)=E, V'(r*)<0, V<E beyond r*, |r| >= r*) with compact continuation and the uniqueness of the apsis, which neither source states in this form.

canonical.name: Repulsive Coulomb scattering as a global noncolliding motion: strict monotonicity of V, single simple turning point, asymptotic velocities, half-angle quadrature and the perpendicular asymptotic distance b = J/sqrt(2 mu E)
canonical.support: Both sources give the Coulomb angle formula; the global noncollision statement, the asymptotic velocity limits and the perpendicular-distance computation with the logarithmic longitudinal shift excluded are proved locally, and the CM15 review records that no finite straight-line intercept is claimed.

canonical.name: The action variable of a two-simple-turning-point family is C^1 with derivative T(E)/(2 pi), including the endpoint singularity treatment
canonical.support: Tong's §4.5.3 states the varying-endpoint cancellation informally; the item proves C^1 dependence of the turning points by the inverse function theorem and computes the derivative with the substitutions s = U(q), s = E - z^2 and the Leibniz rule under exact hypotheses.

canonical.name: Ellipse area lamda_2(E_ell) = pi ab and the polar area identity (1/2) int_0^{2 pi} rho^2 dphi, with the Axiom of Countable Choice declared
canonical.support: The geometric area computation and its measure-theoretic justification through the affine change of variables, the polar diffeomorphism and Tonelli are local; the choice declaration is explicit in the statement.
